summary_html: Court issues a **protective or restraining order** to prevent contact, remove abuser, or ensure safety without removing the child. Federal law leaves implementation to states but funds protection efforts through CAPTA and IV-B.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — authorizes protective interventions and state plan requirements  
- **SSA Title IV-B** — permits funding for protective services and court interventions

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Dept. of Human Services v. J. R. F.
key_cases.holding: Without resolving how far the juvenile code authorizes such orders, the court vacated an order requiring a father to make his other, non-ward children available for visitation with his ward, holding the record inadequate because ORS 419B.090(4) makes parental due process rights part of the construction and application of every provision of ORS chapter 419B.
key_cases.relevance: Governs entry of a conduct-regulating order against a parent short of removing a child, and faults the juvenile court for entering one without the findings of fact ORS 419B.449(2) requires.
key_cases.quote: the due process rights of parents are always implicated in the construction and application of the provisions of ORS chapter 419B

key_cases.case_name: Dept. of Human Services v. M. P.
key_cases.holding: The court held a protective custody order under ORS 419B.150 is not an 'initial child custody determination' and the supporting declaration is not the first pleading, so the dependency proceeding commenced when the petition was filed, defeating UCCJEA home-state jurisdiction.
key_cases.relevance: Catalogues the limited protective orders a juvenile court may enter before a jurisdictional hearing without removing the child.
key_cases.quote: An issued but unexecuted protective custody order does not trigger the juvenile court's jurisdiction or commence any time period during which a petition must be filed.
